title: Crispy Garlic Chicken
seoTitle: Asian Chicken Lettuce Cups | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Ginger-garlic ground chicken in crisp butter lettuce with hoisin drizzle
subtitle: Ginger-garlic ground chicken in crisp butter lettuce with hoisin drizzle
description: Ground chicken cooks with ginger, garlic, water chestnuts, and scallions, served in butter lettuce cups with hoisin, lime, and crushed peanuts.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Garlic Chicken in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use green onions as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep lettuce cups
steps.instruction: Wash butter lettuce leaves and dry thoroughly on towels. Keep chilled on a sheet pan until service so cups stay crisp and cup-shaped.

steps.title: Brown ground chicken
steps.instruction: Cook chicken in batches over medium-high 8–10 minutes, breaking into small crumbles until fully cooked with lightly golden edges. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Add aromatics and chestnuts
steps.instruction: Add ginger, garlic, water chestnuts, and half the scallions. Cook 3–4 minutes until fragrant and chestnuts heated through with slight crunch.

steps.title: Finish sauce
steps.instruction: Stir in soy sauce, 2 tbsp hoisin, sesame oil, and vinegar. Simmer 2 minutes until liquid mostly absorbs and mixture looks glossy, not wet.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Crispy Garlic Chicken onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Assemble cups at the line
steps.instruction: Spoon ¼ cup chicken into each lettuce cup. Drizzle hoisin, sprinkle peanuts and scallions, serve with lime. Leaves should crack lightly when bitten.

proTips: Offer rice on the side for crew who want more carbs without changing the core recipe.
Substitute crushed cashews if peanut allergy is a concern at your hall.
Double-stack small leaves for sturdier cups that do not tear when filled.
tonightSpread: Steamed jasmine rice for optional base.
leftovers: Chicken filling over rice bowls next day—skip lettuce.
Wrap filling in rice paper spring rolls with herbs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Low-carb option that does not feel like diet food. Interactive assembly keeps dinner lively after a quiet shift.
mealPrepNotes: Wash and dry lettuce cups early—wet leaves tear when filled. Chop water chestnuts fine for even distribution. Station: Keep lettuce cups on ice until service—they wilt fast near a hot range. Station: Cook chicken in two batches for better browning and texture. Station: Set build station: lettuce, chicken, hoisin, peanuts, lime, scallion.
